about.sense: The app menu's About item and the About window.

absolute-path.sense: A path that starts at the file system root (begins with /).

accent.sense: A diacritic on a letter (é), in the look-alike-names explanation.

access.sense: Being able to reach or open something (macOS privacy access, a server granting access, a device held with exclusive access).

accessibility.sense: The macOS Accessibility settings pane and its features (text size).

account.sense: The user account on a server or service that Cmdr signs in with.

action.sense: Something the user or a command can do in the UI (a dialog's choices, the viewer's context actions, a command's name in the shortcut list, an undoable action).

activate.sense: Entering a license key to turn on a paid license.

add.sense: Putting something into an existing list or report (a folder, a server, a favorite, a note).

advanced.sense: The Advanced section of Settings, and a collapsible Advanced group in a form.

ai-agent.sense: Cmdr's own AI acting on the user's behalf (it sets filters, proposes renames), including the operation log's initiator label.

ai-client.sense: An outside AI app driving Cmdr over its automation interface, named as the source of an operation.

ai-feature.note: Where the English says "the AI" rather than "Cmdr", keep the distinction: Cmdr is the product acting, the AI is the outside model.
ai-feature.sense: The app's AI-powered functions in general, or the outside model acting as the subject of a sentence.

ai-provider.sense: The company or service that runs the AI model Cmdr talks to (OpenAI, Anthropic, a local server).

ai-reply.sense: An Ask Cmdr assistant answer, or an AI provider response.

ai-tool.note: Developer tooling (Android platform tools) is not this concept.
ai-tool.sense: A function the AI can call (list a folder, search), and its status lines.

allow.note: On Android's own USB-debugging dialog the button is the phone's word; quote the vendor's localized label.
allow.sense: Granting permission for something to happen (a rename, cloud AI, a phone trusting the Mac).

already-exists.sense: A name clash: something with that name is already at the destination.

always.note: Distinct from never; don't let a never sentence borrow the always word.
always.sense: A setting or button choice meaning every time (Always send, Always allow).

android-platform-tools.sense: Google's Android SDK Platform Tools package, which ships adb.

android-tools.sense: The Android command-line developer tools installed on the Mac, as a group.

anonymous.sense: Data collected without identifying the user.

answer.note: A device or server answering is `respond`, not this.
answer.sense: The user replying to a prompt Cmdr is waiting on.

api-key.sense: The secret key a cloud AI provider issues for API access.

app.sense: An application in general: Cmdr itself as "the app", another app on the Mac, the app that opens a file, a cloud provider's sync app.

app-bundle.sense: A folder macOS shows as one item (.app, .bundle, .framework).

app-switcher.sense: The macOS Command-Tab app switcher (a reserved system shortcut).

appearance.sense: The Appearance settings section in Cmdr and the macOS Appearance pane.

apple-account.sense: The Apple Account pane in System Settings, and the account itself.

apple-silicon.sense: Apple's M-series chip family, required by some local AI features.

applications-folder.note: Name it the way the localized Finder sidebar does; some locales rename this folder.
applications-folder.sense: The macOS folder that holds installed apps.

apply.sense: Making a chosen setting, selection, or recent query take effect.

approve.sense: Saying yes to an AI-suggested operation before it runs.

archive.sense: A zip, tar, or 7z file that Cmdr can browse like a folder, create, or edit.

archive-chat.sense: Hiding an Ask Cmdr chat from the active list, or restoring it (Gmail-style), with no compression involved.

ask.note: Also the verb in running prose (Cmdr asks you something); the option label is the short imperative.
ask.sense: A setting option meaning "ask me every time".

ask-cmdr.note: Only the chat panel itself carries this name; a sentence that merely describes what the AI does says Cmdr or the AI.
ask-cmdr.sense: The product name of the AI chat panel; stays verbatim in every language.

ask-question.sense: Putting a question to the AI about files, a folder, or the selection.

attachment.sense: A file or folder the user attaches to an Ask Cmdr question.

attribute.sense: A piece of file metadata a file system stores (an extended attribute, a flag).

authentication.sense: A server or volume checking the user's identity: the technical act behind signing in (authentication required, rejected).

available-offline.sense: A cloud file kept downloaded on the Mac, and the command that pins it there.

back.note: A standalone back button in a list you drill into differs from the paired previous/next of a wizard or the Go menu in many locales.
back.sense: Returning to the previous step, screen, or location.

background.note: The English button "Background" is a verb; most languages have no verb for it, so use the in-the-background phrase, never the bare noun (which reads as a picture or color).
background.sense: Letting a running operation or task continue out of sight.

badge.note: Not the gamification sense some term bases give for badge.
badge.sense: A small overlay marker on a file icon or in the title bar showing a state.

batch-rename.sense: Renaming many files at once from a pattern.

blocked.sense: Something held back from proceeding: a proposed rename preflight won't let through, or an access macOS or another process prevents.

bookmark.sense: A saved location in a file manager (not Cmdr's favorites).

brief-view.sense: The multi-column name-only view mode of a pane.

browse.note: "What you're browsing" (whatever the pane shows) is the plain looking-at sense and may take a view verb.
browse.sense: Moving through folders to look at what is there, including stepping into an archive, bundle, phone, or git ref and listing it like a folder.

browse-file-picker.sense: The button that opens the system file picker to choose a file or folder.

buffer.sense: A block of memory Cmdr keeps filled ahead of use or that can fill up and overflow (the viewer's prefetch buffer, the type-to-jump buffer, the file watcher's event buffer).

bug.sense: A defect in Cmdr the user helps find and the developer fixes.

busy.note: A volume someone holds open is in-use; a device with nothing running is idle.
busy.sense: Occupied and unable to take a request right now: a volume with operations running (the greyed menu item's (busy) marker), a device, a provider, a system resource.

button.sense: An on-screen button, named in running text (click the + button).

button-bar.sense: A row of command buttons (Total Commander's drive-button bar).

byte.sense: The byte as a size unit (a byte count, bytes transferred), and raw bytes the viewer shows.

cable.sense: The USB cable that connects a phone, camera, or drive to the Mac.

cache.sense: Locally stored data kept to speed things up.

camera.sense: A digital camera reached over MTP/PTP, or the camera that took a photo.

camera-details.sense: A photo's EXIF block (make, model, exposure).

cancel.sense: Stopping an operation or dismissing a dialog without applying it.

case-sensitive.sense: Whether upper- and lowercase letters count as different.

certificate.sense: A server's TLS certificate that the Mac may or may not trust.

changelog.sense: The document listing what changed in each release.

character.sense: A single text character (in the viewer, in a name, a note's length limit).

character-viewer.sense: The macOS emoji and symbols picker, named in a reserved-shortcut list.

chat.note: Not a technical session; keep any session term for unrelated technical sessions.
chat.sense: One saved Ask Cmdr conversation, and the list of them.

check.note: "Check for updates" is the update concept's phrase, not this one.
check.sense: Verifying something (conflicts before a copy, whether a file changed, the drive index for changes, a key's fingerprint).

checklist.sense: The onboarding list of small optional favors (star, like, email).

chip.sense: A small labeled pill in the UI, such as the repository chip that shows a folder is inside a git repo.

choose.sense: Picking an option from a list or dropdown, or picking an app.

clean-up.note: Deliberately not the delete verb: it sits next to queue rows that literally say deleting.
clean-up.sense: Cmdr tidying away its own half-written or leftover files so nothing looks complete that isn't.

clear.sense: Emptying a field, a search, an index, or a list of recent items without deleting files.

click.note: Many languages split this from pressing a key; a locale that uses one verb for both still records the choice.
click.sense: Pressing the mouse or trackpad button once on a control (a button, a link, a row), as opposed to pressing a key.

client.sense: A program that connects to a server (an AI client over MCP, a sync client).

clipboard.sense: The system pasteboard that cut, copy, and paste use.

close.sense: Closing a window, dialog, tab, or file.

cloud-ai.sense: Sending requests to a remote AI provider rather than a local model; also the consent switch that allows it.

cloud-provider.sense: A file-sync service (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Google Drive) whose folders Cmdr shows.

column.sense: A column of the file list (Name, Size, Ext), a table, or Brief view's multi-column layout.

coming-soon.sense: A marker on a feature or control that isn't available yet but is planned.

command.sense: An action the user can run from the command palette or a menu, or a terminal command.

command-line.sense: A shell command line (a terminal's, or Total Commander's command-line bar).

command-palette.sense: Cmdr's searchable list of every command.

comparator.sense: A comparison sign (<, >, =) in a search filter.

compare-folders.sense: The two-pane command that compares two folders' contents.

complete.note: A scan or an AI answer being finished may take a different word than a file operation; see the locale's note.
complete.sense: An operation or a wizard reaching its end, or a rollback being finished.

compress.sense: Packing files into a new archive (the Compress command, its dialog, and its level setting).

compromised.sense: A server key marked as unsafe (@revoked in known_hosts).

configure.sense: Setting something up (a provider, a configuration profile).

confirm.sense: Verifying that an operation actually landed, or the user confirming a choice.

conflict.sense: A name clash at the destination during a copy or move.

connect.note: A drive physically attached by cable is a different state from a logical connection in some locales.
connect.sense: Establishing or holding a network or device connection (a server, a share, a phone).

context-window.sense: How much text an AI model can take in at once.

continue.sense: Going on with a flow or an operation after a pause or a question.

conversation.sense: One thread of messages between the user and Ask Cmdr, as distinct from chatting as an activity.

convert.sense: Changing a file's contents or format.

copy.note: "A copy" as a noun (the duplicate object) may take a different word than the verb.
copy.sense: Duplicating files to another location (F5), or copying text or a path to the clipboard.

cost.note: Regional spelling splits (es coste / costo) are recorded per locale.
cost.sense: What something takes in money (AI usage) or in resources (disk space, a macOS process to suppress).

crash-report.sense: The diagnostic report Cmdr sends after it stopped unexpectedly or hit a background problem.

create.note: The Created column header is a date label in Finder, not a participle.
create.sense: Making a new folder, file, or archive; also the Created date column.

credentials.sense: A username and password pair used to sign in.

current-folder.sense: The folder the active pane is showing.

cursor.sense: The file-list cursor: the highlighted row that keyboard commands act on (also the viewer's text cursor).

custom.sense: A user-defined value instead of a preset or default.

cut.sense: The clipboard cut command (to paste as a move).

damaged.sense: A file or archive whose contents can't be read correctly.

dark-mode.sense: The macOS light or dark appearance.

dashboard.sense: An AI provider's billing or usage web page.

database.sense: A structured data store (the index database, a provider's database).

date-wilting.sense: The date-color scheme that fades file dates like a wilting plant (green, yellow, brown).

debounce.sense: Waiting for a burst of events to settle before acting on them (an advanced setting).

debugging.sense: Diagnosing problems in Cmdr itself: a debug log level, logs or files kept for debugging.

default.sense: The value or app used when the user hasn't chosen one.

delete.sense: Removing files, either to the trash or permanently; also removing a model or other stored data.

delete-permanently.sense: Deleting without the trash, so the files can't be restored.

deny.sense: Refusing a permission request or a proposed rename.

deployment.sense: An Azure OpenAI deployment: the name a deployed model gets in the user's Azure resource, which may differ from the model name.

desktop.sense: The macOS Desktop folder (named in lists of protected folders), and the Desktop & Dock settings pane.

destination.note: A symlink's target is a different sense (what the link points at).
destination.sense: Where a copy, move, or compress writes to.

details.sense: Further information behind a disclosure (license details, report details).

detect.sense: Noticing a connected device or a condition (a phone plugged in, a symlink loop).

device.sense: An MTP/PTP or USB device such as a phone, Kindle, or camera.

diagnostics.sense: Diagnostic information collected to troubleshoot a problem.

dialog.sense: A dialog window in Cmdr or macOS.

dimensions.sense: An image's pixel width and height.

direct-connection.sense: Cmdr's own fast SMB connection to a share, as opposed to the slower connection macOS mounts.

directory-hotlist.sense: Total Commander's list of frequently used folders (a feature Cmdr doesn't ship).

disable.sense: Switching a setting or feature off.

disconnect.sense: Ending a network or device connection on purpose (a server, a share, an ADB phone).

disk-image.sense: A .dmg or similar file macOS mounts as a volume.

disk-usage.sense: How much of a drive is used, shown as a bar or a figure.

dismiss.note: Must never read as ignore, reject, or erase.
dismiss.sense: Closing a notice, toast, popover, or a finished queue row, with nothing undone, retried, or deleted.

dock.note: Apple drops the article in short labels ("Add to Dock") but keeps it in sentences in some languages.
dock.sense: The macOS Dock, kept as Apple's proper name.

documents.sense: Office and text documents as a file kind.

done.note: The lifecycle status and the screen-reader word after a finished checklist step can legitimately differ.
done.sense: A finished state: an operation's lifecycle status, a wizard's close button, or a checklist step read aloud.

double-click.sense: Clicking twice quickly (to open, or on the pane background to go up).

download.sense: Fetching an update, a model, or a file from the internet; also the Downloads folder jump.

drag.sense: Moving something with the mouse held down (drag and drop, a drag threshold, dragging an icon to the Dock).

drive.sense: A storage device or its volume (internal disk, USB drive, SD card).

duplicate.sense: Copying the selection into the same folder.

edit.note: Three senses share this English word: edit a file in an editor, edit an archive, and edit a saved server's settings (a form). Many locales split them, and the menu bar's Edit menu is Apple's own word.
edit.sense: Opening a file in a text editor (F4), changing a zip's entries, or opening a form to change a saved item.

eject.note: macOS in some languages uses its delete verb for eject; that collides with delete in a file manager.
eject.sense: Safely unmounting a removable drive or disk image so it can be unplugged.

email.note: Placeholder addresses use a reserved example domain; never a registrable one.
email.sense: An email address the user gives Cmdr, or emailing the developer.

empty-trash.sense: Permanently deleting everything in the macOS Trash (Finder's Empty Trash).

enable.note: A Settings label, a hint that tells the user to switch something on, and a reference to a feature that's off may take different shapes.
enable.sense: Switching a setting or feature on.

encoding.sense: A text file's character encoding in the viewer.

encrypted.sense: An archive or entry protected with encryption.

endpoint.sense: The URL of an AI provider's API.

enter-key.note: Also the verb "enter a value"; that sense is not this concept.

entry.sense: One record in a list, an index, a scan, or a credential store (an indexed file, a recent search, a Keychain entry).

error-report.sense: A report about a handled error (not a crash), sent automatically or by the user.

estimate.note: Not the business-quote sense some term bases list first.
estimate.sense: A rough cost estimate for AI usage.

example.note: Many languages split the full word ("Example:") from the abbreviation ("e.g.").
example.sense: A prefix introducing a sample value in a placeholder or hint.

exclude.sense: The user deliberately leaving a folder or file out of indexing or a search scope.

expired.sense: A license that is no longer valid.

exposure.sense: A photo's exposure, aperture, and ISO metadata fields.

extension.note: Not a browser or system extension ("Login Items & Extensions" is a pane name).
extension.sense: The part of a filename after the last dot.

extract.sense: Unpacking files out of an archive.

failed.sense: Something didn't work. Cmdr's voice never labels it with a bare failure or error word.

favorites.sense: Folders the user pinned for quick access, and the Ctrl-D favorites menu.

feedback.sense: A message from the user to the developer (the feedback dialog and menu item).

fetch.sense: Getting a file from a phone, server, or archive into a temporary copy before viewing it.

file.note: The macOS menu bar's File menu is Apple's own localized title and may differ from the ordinary word.

file-handle.sense: An open reference an app, process, or server holds on a file, which keeps it in use.

file-list.sense: The list of files and folders inside a pane.

file-manager.sense: The kind of app Cmdr is.

file-operations.sense: Copy, move, delete, and the like as a group; also a Settings section and card name.

file-system.sense: A volume's on-disk format and structure (APFS, FAT32, exFAT), and the file-system watcher settings.

filter.sense: Narrowing a list or search results by a condition (search facets, the recent-queries filter).

finder.sense: Apple's Finder, kept as a proper name.

fingerprint.sense: The hash that identifies a server's SSH key (SHA256:…).

font.sense: A typeface used to draw text.

force-quit.sense: The macOS Force Quit Applications window and its reserved shortcut.

forget.sense: Dropping something Cmdr remembers (a saved server, a saved password, a trusted host key, a drive's index, Ask Cmdr's notes) without touching any files.

format.note: Several senses: a drive's format, an archive's compression method, and a date or number display format; many locales split them.
format.sense: A disk's file-system format (formatted as exFAT), an archive's compression format, or a display format (dates, sizes).

frame.sense: A video frame, and the frame rate.

free-space.note: The price sense of "free" (no cost) is not this concept.

from-to.sense: The paired source and destination headings of the copy/move dialog, and the scan phase's source label.

full-disk-access.sense: The macOS privacy permission that lets Cmdr read protected folders.

full-view.sense: The detailed column view mode of a pane.

function-key-bar.sense: The row of F-key command buttons at the bottom of the window.

generate.sense: An AI model producing text (stop generating, regenerate).

get-info.note: Apple localizes this label in every language, even where a @key description says to keep it English.
get-info.sense: Finder's Get Info command and window.

git-branch.sense: A git branch, shown in the repository chip and git status and browsable in the .git portal.

git-browser.sense: Cmdr's view that lists a repo's branches, tags, commits, and worktrees like folders.

git-commit.sense: A git commit (a snapshot in the repo's history), as the .git portal lists it.

git-dirty.sense: A git working tree with uncommitted changes.

github-issue.sense: A GitHub issue someone opens to report a problem or request.

github-star.sense: Starring the Cmdr repository on GitHub, whose UI is English-only.

glob.sense: A wildcard filename pattern (*.jpg) in search and selection.

global.sense: A keyboard shortcut scope that works everywhere on the Mac, as opposed to inside the app.

go-back.sense: Navigating backward or forward in a pane's history.

go-to-path.sense: The dialog and command for typing a path to navigate to.

go-to-trash.sense: Opening the trash of the drive the pane is on.

got-it.sense: The acknowledgement button on a notice.

grant.sense: Giving an app a permission (grant full disk access, grant Cmdr access).

group.sense: A labelled group of rows (the volume switcher's Network group), or a Unix file group.

guest.sense: Connecting to a server without an account.

hard-link.sense: A second directory entry for the same file data, so files sharing it are counted once on disk.

help-menu.sense: The menu bar's Help menu, named in prose (send a report from the Help menu).

hex.sense: Base-16 (and base-2) number display in the viewer.

hidden.sense: A file or folder macOS doesn't show by default (dotfiles, the hidden flag).

hide.sense: The app menu's Hide Cmdr and Hide Others commands, and hiding a UI element.

hint.sense: A one-time tip Cmdr shows, and the internal flags that record it was shown.

history.sense: A record of past things: file operations Cmdr ran, a chat's earlier messages, recent searches, closed tabs, git history.

home-folder.sense: The user's home folder (~), and the Go menu's Home item.

host.sense: A network machine Cmdr connects to (an SMB, SFTP, or WebDAV host).

host-key.note: Where the English says only "key" inside the server panel, the context already says whose key it is.
host-key.sense: The SSH key that identifies a server, which the Mac trusts or refuses.

hostname.sense: The network name of a host.

hour.note: Some languages keep the unit singular after a numeral for durations.
hour.sense: Spelled-out durations in a time-remaining line or a countdown.

icloud-drive.sense: Apple's iCloud Drive, which Apple localizes per language.

icon.sense: An app or file icon (in the Dock, in a file row).

idle.sense: Not busy: a device with no transfer running, or a user who stopped typing and clicking.

image.sense: A picture file in technical and label contexts (image indexing, image files).

image-search.sense: Searching pictures by their contents or a description (the image index's search features).

importance.sense: Cmdr's ranking of how much a folder matters to the user, which decides what gets indexed first and feeds AI context.

in-use.note: A full sentence and a grayed-out menu item's short state marker may differ.
in-use.sense: A volume, device, or file that something still has open.

incoming-connections.sense: The macOS prompt to accept incoming network connections.

index.sense: Cmdr's database of a drive's files and folder sizes, and the image index; also the act of building them.

info.sense: Information shown or collected (license info, diagnostic info).

input-source.sense: A macOS keyboard input source (named in a reserved-shortcut list).

install.sense: Installing an update, a tool, or a model.

internet.sense: The internet as a whole, as opposed to a local network (mostly "check your internet connection" advice).

interrupted.sense: Something cut off before it could finish by an outside cause (a signal, a dropped connection).

invert-selection.note: Total Commander and Double Commander have this exact item; the menu item and the palette command share one English string.
invert-selection.sense: The command that flips the selection in the active pane (⇧8): selected files become unselected and the rest selected.

item.note: A menu item or a list entry that isn't a file keeps the ordinary word.
item.sense: A file or folder when the string covers both, or an entry in a scan.

just-now.sense: The newest step of a relative-time label (just now, 5m ago).

keep.sense: Leaving files or a name as they are (the safe answer in a rollback prompt, a rename that kept its name).

key-combination.sense: The actual keys pressed together that a shortcut is bound to, as recorded or named in a conflict warning.

key-file.sense: The private-key file (and its passphrase) the user signs in to an SFTP server with.

keychain.note: Apple localizes Keychain and Keychain Access in many languages; it is not a do-not-translate brand.
keychain.sense: The macOS credential store, its Keychain Access app, and the equivalent keyring on other systems.

keyword.sense: A search term in keyword (not semantic) image search.

kind.sense: A file's type as Finder names it (the Kind column and "select all of the same kind").

language.sense: The UI language, or a natural language in search.

last-used.sense: The column that shows when a saved server was last opened.

later.sense: A button that defers a prompt.

layout.sense: How UI elements are arranged on screen.

learn-more.sense: An info link or button that explains a setting further.

leave-alone.sense: Cmdr deliberately not touching files it can't be sure about during a rollback or undo.

level.sense: A step on a graded setting (compression level, zoom level, log level).

license.sense: A Cmdr license and its tiers (personal, commercial, perpetual).

license-key.sense: The code a user enters to activate a license.

like.note: The comparison word "like" ("apps like TextEdit") is not this concept.
like.sense: Upvoting Cmdr on AlternativeTo, whose UI is English-only.

limit.sense: A cap: a file-system size limit, an AI step or time budget, a list length.

line.sense: A line of text in the viewer, or a line in a config file.

linux-distribution.sense: A Linux distribution, whose package manager provides a missing package.

list.sense: A generic UI list (a server list, the list of apps, a list of results).

load.sense: Reading data into the app or into memory before showing it (loading a folder, a model, suggestions, more rows).

local.sense: On this Mac, as opposed to a server or the cloud (a local model, stored locally).

local-network.sense: The home or office network, the macOS Local Network privacy permission, and finding servers on it.

location.sense: Where a file or command lives on disk, the places listed under a server, or where a photo was taken.

locked.note: Apple localizes the checkbox label; quote it the way the user's Finder shows it.
locked.sense: The macOS Locked flag on a file (the Get Info checkbox) and removing it.

log.sense: Cmdr's on-disk diagnostic log file, and the Logging settings.

look-inside.sense: The AI reading part of a file's contents (text, metadata, thumbnails) to answer a question.

macos-app-names.en: Disk Utility / First Aid / Activity Monitor / Spotlight
macos-app-names.note: Check per locale whether Apple localizes each name; many locales translate some of them.
macos-app-names.sense: macOS app and feature names that Cmdr names in help text.

mailing-list.sense: The occasional-updates email list the user can join from onboarding.

manifest.sense: The list of files included in an error-report bundle.

mcp-server.sense: Cmdr's Model Context Protocol server that AI assistants can connect to.

media-duration.sense: How long a video or audio file plays.

media-playback.sense: Playing video or audio in a preview (play, pause, mute, volume).

memory.note: Two senses: system RAM and Ask Cmdr's remembered notes.
memory.sense: RAM; also Ask Cmdr's saved notes ("memory") in some strings.

menu.sense: A menu in the macOS menu bar, a context menu, or Cmdr's favorites menu.

merge.sense: Combining the contents of two same-named folders in a conflict.

message.sense: A chat message to or from the AI, or a message the user writes.

metadata.sense: Data about a file (tags, permissions, EXIF) rather than its contents.

model-library.sense: A provider's catalog of downloadable models (the Ollama library).

modified.note: The column header and date filters use Finder's date label; the keyboard-shortcuts filter means shortcuts the user changed, with no date involved.
modified.sense: A file's last-changed date (column header, date filter) and the participle for a changed file.

mount.sense: Attaching a network share or disk image to the file system so it appears as a volume.

move.note: "Move to left column" and "moves down" (cursor movement) are not this concept.

move-to-trash.sense: Sending files to the trash (the delete dialog's switch, its confirm button, the queue row).

name.sense: A file's name; also the Name column header and a saved server's name field.

native.sense: Provided by the operating system itself (the macOS SMB connection Cmdr falls back to).

navigate.sense: Going to a folder in a pane (clicking a breadcrumb, jumping to a download, the Navigation settings).

network.sense: A computer network in general (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, the network a server is on, network errors), and the volume switcher's Network group.

network-drive.sense: A NAS or network volume, as a place photos and files live.

network-share.sense: An SMB shared folder offered by a server or NAS.

new-file.sense: The command that creates an empty file.

new-folder.sense: The command that creates a folder (F7).

none.sense: The "no value" option in a picker.

not-finished.sense: An operation that stopped before completing, stated gently (queue status, failure toast).

not-found.sense: Something Cmdr looked for isn't there (a path, a file, a share, a device, a command, the adb binary).

note.sense: Free text the user writes (a note on an error report, the feedback message), or Ask Cmdr's saved notes.

notification.sense: A toast or system notification Cmdr shows.

offline.sense: Without a network connection, or back on one (a model that works offline, a host that comes back online).

on-device.sense: An AI model that runs on this Mac itself, as opposed to a cloud provider's servers.

on-disk.sense: Where a file's data physically lives, on the drive (a file changed on disk, repo data on disk).

on-disk-size.sense: A file's or folder's physical size on the drive (allocated blocks), paired with its content size.

online-only.sense: A cloud file whose contents the provider evicted, leaving only a placeholder on the Mac; opening, copying, or trashing it downloads it first.

notMatch: open this file in an editor
open.sense: Opening a file with its app, entering a folder or server, or showing a window.

open-beta.sense: Cmdr's current public beta phase, named in onboarding, the About window, and the analytics setting.

open-with.sense: Opening a file in a chosen app: the Open With submenu, and opening with the default app.

operation.note: Wider than transfer (copy or move only). A running operation is also where the queue and the log get their names.
operation.sense: The category of file work Cmdr performs: copy, move, delete, trash, rename, folder or file creation, archive edit.

operation-log.sense: The window and feature that record every past file operation, for review and rollback.

operation-queue.sense: The window and list of file operations running or waiting their turn.

options.note: The Option key is the modifier-key concept.
options.sense: A set of choices in a popover, a dropdown, or a settings row.

organization.sense: The company or organization a commercial license is issued to.

original.sense: The source files of a copy or move, which Cmdr keeps where they were until the destination copy is safe.

outdated.sense: An index that may no longer match what's on the drive.

overwrite.sense: Replacing an existing file at the destination with the incoming one.

owner.sense: The account that owns a file or folder (shown in its permissions), or the person who runs a server.

package.sense: A file that bundles other files (.jar, .apk, Office documents), or a Linux software package.

page.sense: A page of a PDF or of a web site, and the Page Up / Page Down navigation.

pane.note: A System Settings pane ("the Privacy & Security pane") is Apple's term, not this concept.
pane.sense: One of Cmdr's two side-by-side file panels.

password.sense: A secret the user types to sign in or unlock an archive.

password-protected.sense: An archive that needs a password to open.

paste.sense: The clipboard paste command, and saving clipboard content as a file.

pattern.sense: A text pattern that names are matched against or renamed by (a glob or regex in search and selection, a rename pattern).

pause.sense: Temporarily halting a running operation or indexing pass.

percent.sense: A percentage, spelled out for screen readers.

permission.note: Consent to share data is a different sense in some locales.
permission.sense: File-system rights to read or change a file.

personal-data.sense: Information that identifies the user or their files.

phone.sense: An Android phone reached over ADB or MTP.

photo.sense: A picture in warm, user-facing copy (network-drive photo archives, searching your photos).

pin.sense: Keeping a tab, a server row, or Cmdr's Dock icon in place, and releasing it.

placeholder.note: Two senses under one English word; a language may need two words. Unrelated to the catalog's {name} placeholders.
placeholder.sense: A stand-in to replace with a real value: the example text in an empty input field, or a token in a format string or URL (YYYY, an Azure endpoint's resource name).

port.sense: A network port number, or a USB port.

preferences.sense: An OS or device Preferences label the user must find (Android's USB Preferences).

preset.sense: A predefined value in a settings picker.

preview.note: Apple's Preview app is a proper name that follows the localized app name.
preview.sense: A quick look at a file's contents without opening it in an app (the noun and the verb).

previous-next.sense: A paired previous/next control (wizard steps, search matches, the Go menu).

problem.note: Cmdr's voice avoids a bare error word; this is the neutral noun for what went wrong.
problem.sense: A non-fatal issue named in explanatory prose, in Cmdr's calm voice.

process.sense: A running program or system daemon.

progress.sense: How far a running operation has got.

prompt.sense: A dialog asking the user something (a system prompt), or the text sent to an AI model.

properties.sense: A file's properties window on non-Mac systems.

protocol.sense: A network protocol (SMB, SFTP, WebDAV, MTP).

put-back.sense: Returning trashed items, or old file names, to where they were.

query.sense: What the user typed into search or selection.

quick-look.note: Apple localizes this feature name in many languages; follow the localized Finder.
quick-look.sense: Apple's Quick Look feature and its menu action.

quit.sense: The app stopping (Quit Cmdr, the quit gate, quit unexpectedly).

quit-and-reopen.sense: The macOS button that relaunches an app after a permission change.

quota.sense: A storage or usage allowance that has run out.

rate-limit.sense: An AI provider refusing or throttling requests because too many came too fast.

read-only.sense: A volume, device, or archive that can be read but not changed.

ready.sense: Prepared and available (an index, a model, an update).

recent.sense: Recently used or newest items (recent paths, searches, selections, the palette's Recent group, recently closed tabs, the latest download).

reclaim.sense: Freeing disk space by deleting something Cmdr stored (a model, an index).

recommended.sense: The suggested option in a choice.

reconnect.sense: Restoring a dropped connection to a server, drive, or device.

redact.sense: Removing private details from logs before a report is sent.

redo.sense: Reapplying the last undone text edit.

reference-id.sense: The ID a sent report gets so the user can refer to it.

refresh.sense: Re-reading a folder or list from disk.

regex.sense: A regular expression: the Regex mode of the search and selection bars, and a pattern written in it.

register-shortcut.sense: Whether macOS accepted (registered) a system-wide keyboard shortcut for Cmdr.

reject.sense: Saying no to an AI-suggested operation.

release-notes.sense: Notes describing what changed in a release.

relevance.sense: How well a search result fits the query (the search-results sort order).

reload.sense: Reading a file again in the viewer.

remote.sense: On another machine (a remote folder on a server).

removable.sense: A drive built to be ejected and unplugged (USB stick, SD card), as opposed to an internal disk.

remove.sense: Taking something out of a list or setting (a favorite, a host, a folder from indexing) without deleting files.

rename.sense: Changing a file's name (the command, the act, and a single name change as a noun).

rename-cycle.sense: A set of renames that swap names in a loop, so one needs a temporary name.

renew.sense: Extending a subscription license for another period.

replace.sense: Putting one thing in place of another (an existing file, an archive).

reply.sense: The AI's answer in an Ask Cmdr chat, or a logged model response.

report.sense: A diagnostic report sent to the developer (crash or error).

report-bundle.sense: The packaged set of logs and details that makes up an error report, saved to disk for debugging.

repository.note: English uses both the short "repo" and the full "repository"; a locale may mirror that register split.
repository.sense: A git repository Cmdr detects and browses (the repository chip, the .git portal), and Cmdr's own repository on GitHub.

request.sense: A call sent to an API, a server, or a tool (an AI request, a permission request).

reserved.sense: A key combination or name the system keeps for itself.

reset.note: Not a network connection being reset.
reset.sense: Putting a setting, a shortcut, or the zoom level back to its default value.

respond.sense: A device, server, or share answering a request (or not).

restart.sense: Restarting the app or the Mac.

restore.sense: Getting a file or an earlier state back from somewhere that kept it (a document revision, a cloud service's trash, a backup).

resume.sense: Continuing a paused operation or indexing pass.

retry.sense: Attempting the same action once more.

review.note: A plain look-over with no decision ("see a history") is the see concept.
review.sense: Going through proposed changes to approve or deny each (an approval gate).

revoke.sense: Taking back a permission or a key that was granted before.

rollback.sense: Undoing a running or finished copy or move by deleting what it wrote or moving files back.

root-folder.sense: The ceiling folder of a saved server, a volume's top folder, and the folder a pane opens in.

rotate.sense: Turning an image left or right.

row.sense: A row in the file list, a queue, or a table.

running.note: An operation in progress and a local AI server that is up can legitimately take different words.
running.sense: A task or operation currently in progress; also a server process that is up.

runtime.sense: The software environment the local AI model runs in, which Cmdr downloads and installs before a local model can run.

save.sense: Storing something (a file, a setting, a password) so it persists.

save-panel.sense: The macOS Save dialog Cmdr opens to save content as a file.

scan.sense: Walking a drive or folder to find and count its files (drive indexing, the pre-copy count).

scope.sense: Where a search looks, or where a keyboard shortcut applies.

screen.sense: A display, or a phone's screen.

screenshot.sense: macOS screenshots and screen recording (reserved system shortcuts).

search.note: The button that starts a search and the feature's name can take different forms.
search.sense: Finding files by name or content (the Search dialog, the button that runs it, the Settings section).

search-match.note: "Matches the pattern" (a verb) is not this concept.
search-match.sense: A search result, or a hit inside the viewer's text search.

see.note: The macOS menu bar's View menu is Apple's own localized title.
see.sense: Looking at something without acting on it ("See 12 favorites", "See a history"), and the F3 view command.

select.sense: Marking files in a pane for an operation, and the resulting set.

send.note: A button, a dialog title, and a verb in prose can take different forms.
send.sense: Sending a report, feedback, or data to the developer or an AI provider.

server.sense: A network machine offering files (SMB, SFTP, WebDAV), or a local AI server.

server-address.sense: The URL or hostname the user types to reach a server.

service.note: The macOS app menu's Services submenu is Apple's own localized title.
service.sense: An online service (an AI provider, a cloud-sync service).

settings.sense: Cmdr's Settings window and its sections.

share-menu.sense: The Share submenu that hands files to other apps (AirDrop, Mail).

sharing-and-permissions.sense: The section of Finder's Get Info window that lists who can read and write an item.

shortcut.sense: A key combination that runs a command.

show.sense: Making something visible (Show hidden files, Show favorites, Show all).

show-in-finder.sense: The macOS command other apps use to reveal a file, which Cmdr can answer.

side-panel.sense: The panel beside the file panes that holds Ask Cmdr.

sidebar.sense: A window's sidebar (Finder's, and the Settings window's).

sign-in.sense: Authenticating to a server or service.

sign-out.sense: Not (or no longer) authenticated; also logging out of the Mac.

sign-up.sense: Joining the occasional-updates mailing list, or creating an account with a provider.

similar.sense: Image-similarity search: finding pictures that look like a given one.

size.sense: A file's or folder's size (the column header, folder-size calculation).

skip.sense: Leaving one item out of an operation (a conflict answer, a per-item outcome).

slideshow.sense: Showing images one after another full screen.

slow.sense: A volume or connection that answers slowly.

snapshot.sense: A frozen point-in-time copy: a git commit seen as a folder, or an APFS snapshot folder search skips.

software.sense: Programs, and the hardware they run on.

sort.sense: Ordering the file list by a column.

source.note: Open-source and a reference source are not this concept.
source.sense: Where a copy or move reads from.

source-available.note: Never translate as "open source": that claim is false for Cmdr.
source-available.sense: Cmdr's license model: the code is public to read under the BSL, which isn't an open-source license.

speed.sense: How fast a transfer or a connection goes, and making it faster.

stack-trace.sense: The list of code locations active when a crash happened.

stall.sense: A transfer or file fetch that is still alive but has made no progress for a while.

status.sense: The current state of something (a server, a license, a git file, an index, a sync app), as a label, column, dot, or badge.

status-bar.sense: The bar at the bottom of a pane or the viewer showing counts and state.

step.sense: One numbered stage of the onboarding wizard, a setup guide, or an install (Step 2 of 4).

stop.sense: Halting something that runs (a search, a local AI server, an operation during rollback).

storage.sense: Space to store data (a phone's storage, cloud storage, the Storage pane).

store.sense: Where data or a name physically lives (a destination that can't store a name, a file stored on a drive, a password stored in the keychain).

streaming.sense: The viewer's mode that reads a huge file in pieces instead of loading it whole.

striped-rows.sense: Alternate row shading in the file list.

subscription.sense: A time-limited commercial license the user renews, as opposed to a perpetual one.

suggestion.sense: Something proposed to the user (AI-suggested operations, combobox suggestions).

supported.sense: Whether a volume, OS version, or feature is handled.

swap-panes.sense: Exchanging the left and right panes.

symlink.sense: A file-system link that points at another path.

sync.sense: Keeping two copies in step (a cloud folder with its provider, live-synced settings).

system-integrity-protection.sense: The macOS protection that keeps system files unchangeable.

system-settings.sense: The macOS System Settings app (usually a runtime placeholder in the source).

system-settings-pane.sense: System Settings pane names hardcoded in a few error suggestions (General, Login Items & Extensions, Storage).

tab.sense: A tab in a pane (several folders per pane).

tag.sense: A Finder color tag on a file.

tail.sense: The viewer's follow-the-end mode, like tail -f.

tap.sense: Touching a button on a phone's screen.

technical-details.sense: The disclosure under an error message that holds the raw system code and message, which suggestion text points at.

terminal.sense: A terminal app in general, and Apple's Terminal app by name.

text-editor.sense: The app that opens a file for editing (F4).

theme.sense: Cmdr's light, dark, or follow-the-system appearance setting.

this-computer.note: Regional vocabulary splits here (es ordenador / computadora / equipo); a locale records its pan-regional choice.
this-computer.sense: The user's own computer, named generically (not Mac) because the sentence also runs on Linux or means any machine.

this-mac.note: Apple's prose names the machine with a classifier in several languages; keep "Mac" itself verbatim.
this-mac.sense: The user's own computer, named as the Mac Cmdr runs on ("on this Mac", "stays on your Mac").

threshold.sense: A cutoff value in a setting.

throughput.sense: Data moved per unit of time.

thumbnail.sense: A small preview image of a file.

time-ago.sense: A relative past time (5m ago, a moment ago) in recent-search tooltips and error panes.

time-left.note: "Left" as a direction (left pane) and "left alone" are other concepts.
time-left.sense: Time remaining in a progress readout ("3m left").

timeout.sense: A request that took too long and was given up on.

timestamp.sense: A recorded date and time on an event.

tint.sense: The faint background color Cmdr gives a pane by volume type (local, SMB/SFTP/WebDAV, MTP), and its color palette.

title-bar.sense: The window's title bar (where the Full Disk Access badge sits).

toggle.sense: Switching something between two states (a command label, a settings switch).

token.sense: A unit of AI model input or output that providers bill by.

too-large.sense: A file too big for the destination's file system or for the viewer, or a name too long.

toolbar.sense: A row of buttons at the top of a window or panel.

transfer.sense: A copy or move of data in flight (the transfer progress dialog), narrower than operation.

trust.sense: Accepting a server's key or certificate as genuine.

type.note: "Type" as a keyboard verb (typing text) is not this concept.
type.sense: A server's protocol column, or a file type in general.

typo.sense: A typing mistake (in a license key or email).

udev.sense: Linux device-permission rules needed for MTP access.

undo.note: Three different actions share the English word; many locales need three words.
undo.sense: Reversing the last action (text undo, putting trashed files back, reverting an AI rename run).

unexpected.sense: Something happened that Cmdr didn't anticipate.

unknown.sense: A value Cmdr can't determine (an unknown size, cost, or model).

unlock.sense: Opening a password-protected archive with its password.

unplug.sense: A drive or device physically detached (or dropped off) while Cmdr was using it; also plugged in by cable.

unreachable.sense: A host or share Cmdr can't get to over the network.

untouched.sense: Files Cmdr guarantees it didn't change (the originals after a failed transfer).

up-to-date.sense: At the newest version, or an index that is current.

update.sense: A new Cmdr version, checking for and installing it; also keeping an index current.

upgrade.sense: Moving to a paid license (the upgrade page), or a new onboarding option after an app upgrade.

usage.sense: How much of something was used (AI tokens and spending, anonymous app usage stats).

usb-debugging.note: Quote the phone vendor's localized label; the user finds the switch by that text.
usb-debugging.sense: The Android developer option that lets ADB reach the phone.

user.sense: A person using Cmdr, or a macOS or server user account.

username.sense: The account name used to sign in to a server.

valid.sense: Whether a license key, a name, or a value is acceptable.

view-mode.sense: A pane's layout (Brief, Full) and the View menu that switches it.

volume.sense: A mounted file system as macOS lists it.

volume-switcher.note: English calls it both switcher and chooser; give it one name.
volume-switcher.sense: The dropdown above a pane for picking a drive, favorite, or server.

waiting.sense: Queued and not yet running, or waiting on the user or a device.

wake.sense: Waking a phone's screen or a sleeping Mac.

watcher.sense: The file-system change watcher and the change events it reports.

whats-new.sense: The release-notes window shown after an update.

wildcard.sense: The * and ? characters standing for any text in a filename pattern.

window.sense: An app window (a dialog window, the About window, the queue window, the window edge) and the Window menu.

wizard.sense: A step-by-step setup flow (the onboarding wizard, the AI provider setup).

word-wrap.sense: Wrapping long lines in the viewer.

working-tree.sense: The checked-out files of a git repository, in the ordinary git sense.

worktree.sense: Git's own name for a linked checkout, kept verbatim by the @key descriptions.

write.sense: Data landing on a drive (what a copy has written so far).

zoom.note: The macOS Window menu's Zoom item (fill the screen) is a different, Apple-named action.
zoom.sense: Text and UI scaling in Cmdr (zoom in, out, to a percentage).
